 Order

This petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C by the sole accused in Crime No.109/2022 of Kuknur police station, Yalaburga, Koppala District, registered for offences punishable under Sections 363 and 376 and Section 6 of POCSO Act, 2012.

2. Heard both the sides and perused the material on record.
3.
The case of the prosecution is that, two years back, victim girl aged about 17 years got acquainted with the accused/ petitioner, who used to rear sheep at a farm located near by her house.
After three months, he proposed to her and they got into a relationship.
Thereafter, they used to meet in the fields.
On 01.10.2020 the accused took the victim to a land in Sy. No.485 in Itagi Tanda and committed penetrative sexual assault on her and following that, he repeated the said act 5 to 6 times.
On 20.06.2022 at about 11:00 a.m, accused told the victim to come to Koppal so that they could elope and get married and thus induced the minor victim to accompany him.
He took her in a train from Koppal to Bangaluru and then on 21.06.2022 at 9:30 p.m., took her to Udupi in a bus and left her in the KSRTC bus-stand and went away.

4. The prosecution has alleged that the petitioner has committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim aged about 17 years and kidnapped her and left her in the KSRTC bus-stand in Udupi and went away.
In the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of CR.P.C she has not alleged that the accused has committed any sexual assault on her.
Medical examination of the victim has been conducted.
It is opined that there are no signs suggestive of vaginal penetration but further opined that the possibility of penetrative and non-penetrative sexual assault cannot be ruled out.
It is also mentioned therein that there were no injuries suggestive of application of force at the time of examination.
In the medical report, the history of the incident has been mentioned.
It is stated that no history of sexual intercourse in any of the above stated incident are mentioned.
5. The prosecution has collected the school certificate issued by the Head Master of the Government Primary School of Kukanur in proof of the victim girl.
In the said school certificate of the victim girl date of birth is mentioned as 16.06.2005.

It is therefore contended by the learned High Court Hanumantha S/O Durgappa Poojar vs Smt. Ambika W/O Muttappa Lamani on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97554928/

sentences.text: Government Pleader that the victim was a minor below the age of 18 years as on the date of incident.
However, the learned counsel for petitioner has vehemently contended that the school certificate is not sufficient to prove the age of the victim.

6. Initially, case was registered in crime No.47/2022 of Udupi Women police station and later on the point of jurisdiction, case was transferred and registered as Crime No.109/2022 at Kukanur police station, Koppal District.
7. The investigation is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
The prosecution has to establish the guilt of the accused in a full fledged trial.
Considering the medical examination report as well as the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.
, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, the relief sought by the petitioner can be granted.

8. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER i) Petition is allowed,
ii) Petitioner/ accused shall be released on bail in Crime No.109/2022 of Kuknoor police station, subject to following conditions:
a. Petitioner shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with two sureties for likesum to the satisfaction of the trial Court, b.
He shall furnish proof of his residential address and shall inform the Court if there is any change in the address, c. He shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly, d.
He shall not put any threat or inducement to the victim, e.
He shall appear before the trial Court on all dates of hearing, f. He shall not leave the jurisdiction of the trial Court without prior permission of the learned trial Judge.
